elbulli.title: The elBulli line, the wall
elbulli.story: Cadaqués is a short drive over the hill from Cala Montjoi, where elBulli cooked until 2011, and its best-known modern table comes from that kitchen. Compartir opened on the Riera de Sant Vicenç in 2012, run by the three chefs who later made Disfrutar in Barcelona the world's No.1 in 2024; every plate goes to the middle of the table. Across the harbour, Talla serves flame-grilled oysters with ponzu on a terrace facing the white town and shuts from about November to March. Es Baluard, in the old sea wall since 1967, is run by the founders' grandchildren, and its wine list prints the distance in kilometres to each winery.
elbulli.where: Compartir, Cadaqués; Talla, Cadaqués; Es Baluard, Cadaqués

houses.title: One family, three tables
houses.story: Cadaqués's oldest dining rooms are family businesses, and two of them belong to the same family. Ana Mota opened Casa Anita in 1960, with no written menu and shared tables; she died in June 2025, three days short of ninety, and her children Juanito and Ana Mari now cook. Her son Rafa Martín Mota opened Can Rafa on the Passeig in 1982 with Carmen Faixó, and the family's Celler Martín Faixó on the cape supplies the wine for its lobster rice. Casa Nun has served soupy lobster rice on the little Plaça des Portitxó since 1979, from recipes passed down the family.
houses.where: Casa Anita, Cadaqués; Can Rafa, Cadaqués; Casa Nun, Cadaqués

back.title: One lane back from the sea
back.story: Step one street back from the harbour and the prices drop and the view goes, but the fish is the same catch. La Sirena, on Carrer des Call, cooks scorpionfish with sauce and potatoes, suquet and zarzuela, and serves garoines, the local sea urchins, from January to March. Es Balconet, a small room on Carrer de Sant Antoni, is known for its paella, the black one with squid ink among them, and makes suquet when the boats allow. Neither has a sea view to charge for, and neither needs one.
back.where: La Sirena, Cadaqués; Es Balconet, Cadaqués

edge.title: Beach, hill and cape
edge.story: The edges of Cadaqués eat differently from the harbour. S'Estrop, on the Plaça del Passeig facing the beach, cooks paella, fideuà and fish in a charcoal oven, with a set lunch that includes a rice. Es Bar de Dalt, at the top of the village on the road out, is the locals' bar: artichokes, croquettes and calamari under olive trees beside the football ground, with live music on Thursdays. At the end of the road, beside the lighthouse on mainland Spain's easternmost point, Christopher Little has served curries since 1991 at Restaurant Cap de Creus, in a former Civil Guard barracks; driving up needs a booking.
edge.where: S'Estrop, Cadaqués; Es Bar de Dalt, Cadaqués; Restaurant Cap de Creus, Cadaqués

bars.title: Bars with a past
bars.story: Cadaqués drank with painters long before it fed yachts. The Marítim has stood on the beach since 1935, turned ninety in 2025 and is listed as protected local heritage; its cremat, rum and coffee set alight at the table, is the fishermen's drink of the bay. L'Hostal, on the Passeig, was founded by Marci Pogany and is the bar Dalí favoured; listings date the logo he drew for it to 1975, and its walls still carry his memorabilia, though the nightclub years are over and it cooks full meals now.
